gen-gf-oxanium-fs-alpino: Alpino reads cozy and casual, tall in the body with ascenders that look stubby and curves left wide open at the ends. Oxanium then stands above it like one length of bent tubing, bold and commanding, with a big lowercase.
gen-gf-warnes-fs-familjen-grotesk: Ink strokes that taper off before they touch, with no thick-thin swing at all, give Warnes its rounded-nib swagger. Familjen Grotesk takes the quieter job, a plain sans with bowls left unfinished on one side that keep a paragraph lively.
gen-megrim-fs-hind: Angular and a little futuristic, Megrim draws every stroke ending at one measured thickness, with a c as open as a bent paperclip. And Hind handles the reading, its lowercase nearly matching the capitals in a plain sans line that never turns inward.
gen-mystery-quest-fs-pilcrow-rounded: Pilcrow Rounded is a warm sans-serif with big counters, tall lowercase and letter spaces shrunk to a thin crack, so its curves refuse to close. Mystery Quest sits above it with a bookish, nostalgic lean, and its open jaws echo that openness.
gen-almendra-display-inter: Ornate, bookish flourish up top. Almendra Display has a pronounced x-height and letters that never pinch shut, and Inter follows in sans-serif lines with big counters that breathe, so a long page would feel smooth and tidy.
gen-gf-goldman-fs-nunito: Commanding is how Goldman lands, with widely set letters and round forms like open parentheses behind a big lowercase. But Nunito softens the page below, its sans bowls round and its terminals finishing well clear of the stem.
gen-gf-love-ya-like-a-sister-fs-quicksan: Bold, level and a bit cheeky, Love Ya Like A Sister keeps its ascenders barely above the x-height. Quicksand is the softer half, its tall bowls like blown glass bulbs on lines of identical bar thickness, and that gentle bulb shape is what lingers.
gen-gf-paprika-fs-alpino: Paprika scatters its letters at a distance, with lowercase forms that fill the line like capitals. And Alpino brings a cozy, casual sans-serif body whose tall shapes make the ascenders look short, which gives the pair its friendly grip.
gen-fs-styro-archivo: Styro goes retro and commanding, its letters pressed close with barely a gap. Archivo answers by opening its curves outward, a plain sans with a commanding x-height, so the crowded heading gets room to breathe underneath.
gen-fs-styro-fs-epilogue: Epilogue gives a tall-bodied sans lowercase with stubby ascender tips and curvy, unclamped letters on a wire-like monoline skeleton. But Styro, retro and crammed tight, is the strongest quality here, the closed heading letters making that openness stand out.
